scope: Executable reference semantics for original and repaired C-shim regression; no formal ISA correspondence or complete QCP proof.

configuration.arm: AArch64 Advanced SIMD FMIN/FMAX; FPCR.DN=0,FZ=0,AH=0,RMode=RNE, traps disabled
configuration.flags: Floating exception flags/traps are unobserved and not emulated.

references.title: Official Arm A-profile ISA reference, FMIN/FMAX
RISC-V F2.2 FMIN/FMAX NaN and zero rules

arm_minmax.semantics: Propagate a NaN when either input is NaN. With DN=0 signaling NaNs are quieted; signaling operands precede quiet operands, then operand order. For numeric inputs select numerical min/max; -0 precedes +0.

rvv_minmax.semantics: minimumNumber/maximumNumber on active lanes; exactly one NaN selects the numeric operand, both NaN select canonical 0x7fc00000. -0 precedes +0. Signaling-NaN invalid flag is outside observations.

data_movement.NEON: vld1q reads exactly four raw float representations; vget_low/high chooses lanes 0..1/2..3; stores write exactly four, two, or one lane.
data_movement.RVV: vle/vse read/write exactly vl consecutive float representations. Inactive memory is untouched.
data_movement.layout: By-value structs with uint32_t arrays, four NEON or 32 RVV lanes; no native-hardware ABI or formal-layout claim.

oracle: Independent literal known-bit answer table for each architecture and operation. Numeric ordering in the shim is implemented by integer ordering keys rather than host fmin/fmax; expected answers do not call that logic.
valid_domain: Positive n; each input has n+3 readable floats; each output has n writable floats; readable params; separate objects and no overlap. Counterexamples use quiet NaNs and finite operands within this domain.
provenance: Original source/target pinned at be16280c7812a7459c26c3ce82a47339a3d07718. Current impl/testRVV.c reuses the historical Frama-C repair byte-for-byte; see repair.json.
limitations: C-shim replay rather than Arm/RVV hardware execution
No formal refinement of runtime intrinsic definitions to ISA
Finite checks do not prove universal correctness
Spec is an executable requested observation, not a completed QCP verification package

original_counterexample.reason: One output is NaN and the other is the finite value 1.0; this fails numerical-equality-or-both-NaN even when NaN payload and zero sign are ignored.

repair.algorithm: Keep the original RVV min/max intrinsic; detect each input NaN, compute a quiet NaN using RVV addition, then merge this result for either NaN input.
repair.observation: Numerical equality or both NaN. NaN payload/sign and floating exception flags/traps are not observed.

extra_instructions.name: __riscv_vmfne_vv_f32m8_b4
extra_instructions.semantics: Active lane is true for unordered (either NaN) or numerically unequal inputs; signed zeros compare equal.

extra_instructions.name: __riscv_vfadd_vv_f32m8
extra_instructions.semantics: Active binary32 RNE addition, gradual underflow, canonical quiet NaN for NaN inputs or invalid operations. Exception flags are unobserved.

extra_instructions.name: __riscv_vmerge_vvm_f32m8
extra_instructions.semantics: An active true mask selects the second data operand; false selects the first.

limitations: This is a repair of the RVV implementation, not a change to either architecture min/max intrinsic semantics.
The unconditional extra addition can set different floating exception flags.
Exact Arm NaN payload/sign propagation is not reproduced by canonical RVV NaNs.
Native regression is not a completed QCP or hardware theorem.
